chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa and Fadala ibn Ayyub from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man becomes junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) from the beginning of the night, then sleeps until morning in the month of Ramadan. He said: 'There is no penalty upon him.' I said: But he woke up, then slept until morning. He said: 'Let him fast that day as a penalty (qada').'
As for that which indicates the third category, what he narrated...

key_terms.أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ: From the beginning of the night
key_terms.فَلْيَقْضِ: Let him make up / perform qada
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْ ءٌ: There is no penalty upon him
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: Becomes junub (enters state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person becomes junub before Fajr and sleeps until morning in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between involuntary sleep and negligence in maintaining ritual purity during Ramadan. It establishes that while accidental sleep until Fajh incurs no penalty, waking and returning to sleep requires making up the day as a compensatory fast (qada'), reflecting the Shia emphasis on intentionality in ritual impurity.
